visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Atlas pays 1,000 for Cedar. Book net assets are 300, write-ups to fair value 400, and the tax rate 25%. How much goodwill?
questions.explain: Fair value of net assets is 300 + 400 − 100 of deferred tax = 600, so goodwill is 1,000 − 600 = 400. Using book value gives 700; forgetting the tax gives 300.
questions.explain_at: So fair value of net assets is three hundred

questions.q: Under international rules, what does a listed company do with goodwill each year?

options.text: Tests it for impairment, at least annually
Amortises it over its useful life
Depreciates it like factories and equipment
Revalues it upward when the business grows

questions.explain: Goodwill isn't amortised under international rules, or American rules for listed companies; it's tested for impairment at least once a year.
questions.explain_at: Under international rules, and American rules for listed companies, goodwill isn't amortised

questions.q: Goodwill is impaired by 100 and the impairment isn't tax deductible. What happens to cash?
questions.explain: The impairment is non-cash: net income falls 100, and it's added back on the cash flow statement. The cash left when the buyer paid.
questions.explain_at: add the impairment back because it's non-cash

questions.q: Of the $52.6bn Kraft Heinz paid for Kraft, roughly how much was booked as goodwill?
questions.explain: Net assets at fair value were about $22.2bn, leaving about $30.5bn of goodwill. $15.4bn was the 2019 impairment, which also hit trademarks.
questions.explain_at: about thirty point five billion, was booked as goodwill

questions.q: Silence Therapeutics has an equity value of about $1.3bn and an enterprise value of $1.1bn. What does the gap tell you?
questions.explain: Enterprise value is equity value plus debt minus cash, so a lower enterprise value means net cash. Reading it as debt was Sofia's slip.
questions.explain_at: When it's lower, the company has net cash
